facts.text: Shishmaref got its name from the inlet named by Otto von Kotzebue after a crew member, and the village post office opened in 1901.
Herbie Nayokpuk, known as the 'Shishmaref Cannonball,' finished the Iditarod many times, including a second-place finish.
Erosion at Shishmaref, driven by melting permafrost and rising seas, has been receding up to 10 feet per year, threatening homes and infrastructure.
Shishmaref plans to relocate several miles south to Tin Creek, but the site was rejected because melting permafrost made it unsuitable, so a relocation coalition seeks funding.
Shishmaref lies within the Bering Land Bridge National Preserve, a protected area preserving the historic land bridge that once connected Asia and North America.
Sarichef Island, where Shishmaref sits, is part of a 100‑km-long barrier island chain that records 2,000 years of human and environmental history.
